lead.hed: An F-35C trapped on the future John F. Kennedy for the first time
lead.insight: DVIDS posted a Navy photograph of an F-35C Lightning II, attached to the Salty Dogs of Air Test and Evaluation Squadron (VX) 23, making an arrested landing on the flight deck of PCU John F. Kennedy (CVN 79). The caption says it is the first time an F-35C has landed on a Ford-class aircraft carrier. The ship is underway in the Atlantic conducting Aircraft Compatibility Testing of its launch and recovery gear. The photograph was taken Oct. 13 by Mass Communication Specialist Seaman Kaitlyn Bailey. USNI News reported Wednesday that Navy video and imagery show the same trap on Tuesday.

political.hed: Heritage says a census change is the sharper fight against cultural division
political.insight: Wednesday's Heritage commentary says the Trump administration has made bold moves against cultural balkanization, citing fights with the Smithsonian Institution and the educational establishment. It says no move is more vital than the proposal to eliminate race, ethnicity, and sexual preference from the census.

political.hed: A Law & Liberty essay asks what classical liberals want from civic education
political.insight: Thursday's Law & Liberty essay says civics centers that teach Western civilization and great books are often called conservative, and that the writer has not seen political litmus tests in them. It quotes Michael Oakeshott that every person is born heir to an inheritance that can be taken up only by learning. The essay says liberal learning frees students from the present by handing them that inheritance, then asks how civic education sits with classical liberalism and the role of the state.

tech.hed: Army officers say drone work is now a basic soldier skill
tech.insight: Defense News reported Thursday that Army officials at the Association of the United States Army meeting said soldiers training for multi-domain operations need a common baseline they called new basics. In the 2nd Cavalry Regiment that list covers unmanned aerial systems, counter-drone systems, and unmanned ground vehicles. Col. Timothy Price, the regiment commander, said in a Tuesday Army release that counter-drone defense cannot stay tied to static positions if the American way of war is maneuver. The regiment is expanding Project Flytrap from small-unit trials to a battalion-level capability on Europe's eastern flank. Flytrap 5.0, in Lithuania, tested more than 50 industry systems against a live opposing force with the United Kingdom and Australia.

tech.hed: A Public Discourse essay says originalism now cuts against Burkean caution
tech.insight: Thursday's Public Discourse essay recalls Thomas Merrill's 1990s argument that Robert Bork's originalism and Edmund Burke's conservatism were not the same thing, and that Burke beat Bork for anyone who put stock in conservative values. The writer says originalism is more sophisticated in the academy and more common on the Court than it was then, and that the older criticism is more urgent now because originalist jurisprudence has become a threat to conservative commitments.

culture.hed: First Things says Leo's death-penalty post sits against older Catholic teaching
culture.insight: Thursday's First Things essay quotes Pope Leo XIV's Oct. 10 message that the death penalty is inadmissible because it attacks the inviolability and dignity of the person, and that detention can protect citizens without closing off redemption. The essay says that language comes from Pope Francis's 2018 revision of the Catechism, which also records that legitimate authority long treated capital punishment after a fair trial as an acceptable means of safeguarding the common good. It says that older view runs through Scripture, the Fathers and Doctors, and the popes through Pius XII.

watch.hed: Japan's Joint Staff says Liaoning's group was in the Philippine Sea
watch.note: USNI, Wednesday: the People's Liberation Army Navy Liaoning Carrier Strike Group was operating in the Philippine Sea as of Wednesday, according to a Japan Joint Staff Office. The group, led by CNS Liaoning (16), was spotted 155 miles south of Ishigaki Island launching and recovering aircraft.
